meta.title: Pre-decision question register - what must be answered before a sell-vs-renew decision can reasonably be made

legend.answered: Answered from official sources read on 2026-11-11 (source id given).
legend.owner-private: Only the owner or the owner's advisers hold this. Cannot be discovered from public data.
legend.procurable: Can be obtained from a specific document or third party; method given.
legend.unresolvable: Inherently unknowable in advance; handle by scenario, not by forecasting.

questions.question: What is the contract rent, and what are the exact lease expiry date and annual escalations?
questions.impact: Decisive. Every NPV, breakeven and cap-rate calculation in every workbook substitutes an assumption for this. Without it no number on this site is property-specific.
questions.how_to_resolve: Lease document or tenant estoppel certificate; title company lease abstract.

questions.question: What renewal / extension option terms does the lease grant (option period, option rent, notice windows)?
questions.impact: Decisive for renew-vs-sell. An in-the-money option changes the negotiation leverage completely.
questions.how_to_resolve: Lease document, options memorandum, or estoppel.

questions.question: What is the owner's tax basis and equity position (and any secured debt, prepayment penalties, defeasance cost)?
questions.impact: Decisive for after-tax sale proceeds and for whether a Section 1031 exchange is worth executing.
questions.how_to_resolve: Settlement statement of acquisition, loan documents, owner's tax adviser.

questions.question: What is the current appraised value / going-in cap rate for this asset?
questions.impact: Decisive. All published breakevens (6.52%, 6.97% across workbooks) are only usable against a real cap-rate quote.
questions.how_to_resolve: MAI appraisal or two broker opinions of value dated within 90 days.

questions.question: Is the parcel inside City of Los Angeles limits (Measure ULA applies) or in unincorporated county (no city DTT, no ULA)?
questions.impact: High. City sale adds 0.45% base DTT plus 4.0% or 5.5% ULA on top of the 0.11% county DTT - roughly 4.6% to 6.1% of price if in the city.
questions.how_to_resolve: Title report legal description; City of LA boundary lookup; county assessor parcel map.

questions.question: What premium or discount would a buyer pay today for 5, 10 or 15 years of remaining term (WALT)?
questions.impact: High. The whole extend-then-sell thesis rests on term commanding a cap-rate spread; it must be evidenced, not assumed.
questions.how_to_resolve: Broker price opinion with term scenarios; closed comparable sales of NNN assets with similar WALT.

questions.question: Will the tenant (Jack in the Box) sign an extension, and on what rent and guaranty terms?
questions.impact: Decisive for the recommended dual-track plan. The tenant's Q3 FY2026 systemwide sales -1.1% and net closures (-13 in the quarter) signal franchisee stress that may limit rent growth accepted.
questions.how_to_resolve: Confidential extension inquiry to tenant real-estate / franchise development; estoppel with extension checkbox.

questions.question: What is the current property insurance quote (wind/fire/earthquake) and is coverage renewable at acceptable terms?
questions.impact: High. Insurance is a direct NOI deduction and a black-swan absorber; California market availability has been the swing factor for many 2025-fire-adjacent assets.
questions.how_to_resolve: Current renewal quote or independent broker quote; loss-run history.

questions.question: What are the parcel's hazard determinations (CAL FIRE FHSZ, FEMA flood zone, seismic site class / Alquist-Priolo zone)?
questions.impact: Medium-high. Drives insurance cost, lender terms and buyer pricing.
questions.how_to_resolve: CAL FIRE FHSZ map lookup by APN; FEMA Flood Map Service Center; geotechnical report.

questions.question: What did the most recent property tax bill show as assessed value (factored base year value) and any direct assessments?
questions.impact: Medium. Sets the buyer's carry and the Prop 13 reset arithmetic on a sale.
questions.how_to_resolve: Copy of the current secured tax bill; assessor's roll lookup by APN.

questions.question: What replacement properties and yields are actually available for a Section 1031 exchange (45-day identification, 180-day close)?
questions.impact: Decisive for the sell-now branch. A sell decision without a replacement pipeline converts a deferral into a tax bill.
questions.how_to_resolve: Exchange accommodator inventory; broker tape of qualified properties; confirm deadlines with tax counsel (Form 8824 instructions, S18).

questions.question: What federal and California tax rates apply to this owner on a taxable sale (LTCG, NIIT, CA top rate)?
questions.impact: High. After-tax sale proceeds drive the sell-now branch; not read from an official IRS/FTB page on this access date.
questions.how_to_resolve: Owner's tax adviser; IRS and FTB publications for the owner's filing status.

questions.question: How large is the local consumer and employment base the restaurant draws from?
questions.answer: City population 3,869,089 (Jul 2025); county 9,694,934; county personal income $818.5B (2024, highest in the U.S.); metro nonfarm employment 6,282.1k with +30.2k (+0.5%) over 12 months.
questions.impact: Context: a very large, slowly shrinking but currently re-hiring consumer base.

questions.question: Is the local labour market tightening or loosening?
questions.answer: Loosening then re-tightening: metro unemployment 4.4% in Sep 2026 (was 5.5% a year earlier); California 5.1%, US 4.0%. Leisure and hospitality +1.5% YoY.
questions.impact: Positive for restaurant sales; wage pressure remains via ECI +3.9% YoY and minimum wages $16.90 state / $18.42 city / $20.00 fast food.

questions.question: Is the population base growing or shrinking?
questions.answer: Shrinking at the city and county level on the Census Vintage 2025 series: city -0.8% and county -3.2% from the Apr 2020 base to Jul 2025. The CA DOF path cited in the City of LA / LAEDC report has the county below 9.5 million by 2034.
questions.impact: Negative long-run demand headwind for the region; argues against passive long holds without rent growth.

questions.question: What are the current benchmark interest rates?
questions.answer: 10-year Treasury 4.88% (observation 2026-11-09); federal funds target upper limit 4.00% (2026-11-10).
questions.impact: Sets the reinvestment benchmark every hold-vs-sell comparison must beat.

questions.question: What would a sale cost in transfer taxes?
questions.answer: County DTT 0.11% ($1.10 per $1,000). If inside City of LA: base 0.45% plus ULA 4.0% (price $5.4M-$10.9M) or 5.5% (price >= $10.9M), i.e. 4.45% / 5.95% city total, on top of the county 0.11%. Thresholds effective for closings after 2026-06-30.
questions.impact: A city-location sale carries roughly 4.6%-6.1% of price in transfer taxes alone - a first-order input to sell-now.

questions.question: Can a sale be tax-deferred?
questions.answer: Yes, if structured as a Section 1031 like-kind exchange of real property held for business or investment (IRS Form 8824 instructions, 2026).
questions.impact: Makes the sell-now branch viable without immediate capital-gains tax - subject to Q11 and Q12.

questions.question: What is the tenant's latest reported operating trend?
questions.answer: Jack in the Box Q3 FY2026 (ended 2026-07-05): system same-store sales -1.1%, systemwide sales -1.4%, 13 net restaurant closures in the quarter, restaurant count 2,115; adjusted EBITDA $61.2M; refinancing completed.
questions.impact: Tenant is stabilizing but still contracting system-wide; franchise-level margin fell to 37.4% from 39.3%. Extension leverage is moderate, not strong.

questions.question: How bad could a local natural disaster be?
questions.answer: Recent precedent: the January 2025 Eaton and Palisades fires burned 14,021 and 23,448 acres, destroyed 9,414 and 6,837 structures, and caused an estimated $5.2-$10.1 billion of lost economic output. Seismic: USGS gives the Los Angeles region a 60% probability of a M6.7+ earthquake within 30 years (46% for M7.0+, 31% for M7.5+).
questions.impact: Black-swan losses are real and documented; insurance (Q08) and parcel hazard class (Q09) determine how much of it lands on this owner.

questions.question: What do schools look like (family-demographic context)?
questions.answer: LAUSD is California's largest district, enrollment 497,105 (2025-26), English learners 16.4%; statewide enrollment 5,731,260. City bachelor's-degree attainment 38.5%.
questions.impact: Context only for a QSR parcel; no direct lease input.

questions.question: What is the local job-growth forecast?
questions.answer: The City of LA / LAEDC report (May 2024) forecasts real gross county product growth of 1.4% (2024f) and 1.5% (2025f) - a slow-growth path - and cites continued county population decline. BLS actuals show metro employment +0.5% YoY through Sep 2026. Numeric job forecasts through 2028 were not extracted line-by-line this session.
questions.impact: Slow-growth local economy: supports steady-but-unexciting NOI assumptions.
questions.how_to_resolve: Re-read the forecast tables in S20 or the latest LAEDC forecast release for exact job totals.

questions.question: What happens to property taxes after a sale?
questions.answer: Proposition 13: 1% general levy plus voter-approved debt; assessed value grows at most 2%/year; a change of ownership (sale) resets base year value to market value (BOE LTA 2025/023).
questions.impact: A buyer at today's price carries a reset tax basis - priced into buyer's yield; the seller's historic low basis is lost on a taxable sale.

questions.question: What wage floor will the restaurant operator face?
questions.answer: California $16.90/hr (2026-01-01), City of LA $18.42/hr (2026-07-01), California fast food $20.00/hr (AB 1228, effective 2024-04-01).
questions.impact: Compressed franchisee margins reduce the tenant's appetite for rent increases at renewal.

questions.question: What will cap rates be in 2030-2035?
questions.impact: Inherently unknowable. Handled by scenario grid and Monte Carlo in the projection model, not by point forecast.
questions.how_to_resolve: Track: 10-year Treasury (S03), Fed path (S04), net-lease transaction evidence.

questions.question: Will a wildfire, earthquake or recession hit this asset before expiry?
questions.impact: Inherently unknowable. Handled as priced hazards: documented base rates where official (S16), scenario stress where not.
questions.how_to_resolve: Mitigate via insurance (Q08), FHSZ (Q09), and sizing the position - not via prediction.

questions.question: Will Measure ULA or Proposition 13 be amended before a sale?
questions.impact: Legislative risk. ULA thresholds already re-index annually by chained CPI (S06).
questions.how_to_resolve: Monitor City of LA Office of Finance and BOE publications; price a change-of-law contingency into any long-dated hold.

questions.question: Do the published workbooks agree on the recommendation?
questions.answer: Broadly yes on shape, no on numbers: the dominant recommendation across the fifteen prior workbooks is a sequence - open an extension / blend-and-extend conversation now, and keep a Section 1031 sale ready - rather than a passive hold or an unconditional sale. Published breakeven cap rates differ (6.52%, 6.97%, and a ~6.8% asset-yield framing) because each workbook assumes different rent growth, exit caps and costs.
questions.impact: The qualitative plan is robust across independent analyses; the quantitative triggers must be re-solved once Q01-Q04 are known.

questions.question: Is there any official single-tenant QSR cap-rate series to anchor pricing?
questions.answer: No. No government publisher issues this series; it must come from appraisals and broker evidence (Q04, Q06).
questions.impact: Any cap-rate number in any workbook is an assumption or a private quote, never an official statistic.

questions.question: What is the owner's liquidity needs, risk tolerance and concentration limit for this asset?
questions.impact: Decisive for the individual: the same cash flows can be correct for a diversified holder and wrong for someone whose net worth is concentrated in this parcel.
questions.how_to_resolve: Owner's own statement of objectives; adviser conversation. Not modelable from public data.
